meta.title: Source-backed marathon training program rules
meta.design_goal: Create individualized, progressive marathon preparation without disguising population evidence or operational defaults as guarantees.
meta.heuristic_policy: The 5% default weekly build and level volume bands are conservative operational defaults, not proven biological thresholds. They must be anchored to the athlete's recent completed training and reduced when readiness deteriorates.

foundation.purpose: Establish consistent easy volume, tissue tolerance, technique, and strength before adding dense quality work.

build.purpose: Develop threshold, aerobic power, running economy, and long-run durability with controlled progression.

specific.purpose: Rehearse marathon-effort blocks, long-run fuelling, race equipment, and even-effort pacing without turning every long run into a race.

taper.purpose: Reduce accumulated fatigue while retaining short intensity exposures, race rhythm, and normal training frequency where tolerated.

recovery.talk_test: Unrestricted conversation; breathing feels easier than normal easy running.

easy.talk_test: Full sentences; finish with clear reserve.

steady.talk_test: Short sentences; controlled and never straining.

marathon.talk_test: Short phrases; rhythm is controlled and sustainable.

threshold.talk_test: A few words at a time; repeatable, not a time trial.

interval.talk_test: Single words during work; form and repeatability set the limit.

yellow.action: Reduce total work by 20-30%, remove fast finish work, or replace intervals with easy running.

red.action: Stop planned running; use rest or gentle mobility and seek qualified help when symptoms warrant it.

red_flags: severe or unusual shortness of breath
professional_supervision: known cardiovascular, metabolic, or renal disease
return after major injury or surgery

rules: Start fuelling early and use only products and doses rehearsed in long runs.
Build toward the target range progressively; gastrointestinal tolerance overrides the theoretical maximum.
Hydration is individualized to thirst, weather, sweat rate, body size, and aid-station access; do not drink beyond losses.
Sodium does not prevent hyponatremia when fluid intake is excessive.

race_pacing.default_strategy: Even effort with low pace variability. Do not bank time in the opening kilometres.
race_pacing.course_adjustment: Let pace change for hills, wind, heat, and congestion while keeping effort and fuelling controlled.
